resources.string: No tickets yet. Import a PDF or a pass to get started.
Once somebody imports this file they hold the ticket barcode. It cannot be taken back afterwards.
Check that both phones show the same six digits.
Enter your vault passphrase to see your tickets.
You claimed this ticket while offline. It is not final yet: it is confirmed once the device can synchronise.
The sender of this file could not be verified.
The file could not be read. The sender may no longer be allowing access to it.
Tickets do not always come one per page: some PDFs put two on a sheet and others lead with instructions. Check this before saving it.
No barcode was found on this page.
This page holds more than one barcode; the split is a guess.
This barcode already appears on another page. Saving both would create the same seat twice.
Looking for other phones on the same Wi-Fi.
Being on the same network identifies nobody: anyone can advertise under any name. That is why the six digits have to be compared.
Compare with both phones in front of you
You must both see exactly the same six digits. If they differ, somebody is in the middle: do not continue.
%1$d operations were sent to the other phone.
The transfer was cancelled. Nothing moved.
The two phones did not derive the same digits. That means something is relaying the connection. It is not a network fault.
The transfer could not be completed.
A message failed its integrity check.
The connection to the other phone was lost.
The other phone speaks a different version of the protocol.
The conversation did not follow the expected protocol.
The type of this barcode is unknown, so it cannot be drawn. The number above is what counts.
The stored document could not be opened.

You do not need one. The wallet, ingestion, .tkpak files and passing tickets to another phone on the same Wi-Fi all work with no server. A server adds a place for the log to meet devices that are not in the room, and an authority that can settle a contested claim.
Without http:// or https://, https is used.
Enter the code that was emailed to you.
Enter the code from your authenticator app.

The vault passphrase is not your sign-in password. The password proves who you are; the passphrase decrypts your tickets, and the server keeps it nowhere. That is why it is asked for on every connection.
Connected. Syncing exchanges the operation log in both directions.

resources.string: A group is the people you share with more than once: the family, the usual crowd. Sharing an event with a group gives access to whoever is in it at that moment; adding somebody later does not hand them the tickets retroactively.
It has to be an account already registered on this server.
